result:
The only open item is the same `local/role-checks-through-authorization` hit at `apps/react-vite/src/features/users/utils/filter-users.ts:12`. I'm leaving it as it is.

- **Rule:** `local/role-checks-through-authorization` says "Role checks go through `<Authorization allowedRoles={[...]}>` or `useAuthorization().checkAccess`; never compare `user.role` yourself."
- **Why I think it's a false positive:** the line is `role !== 'ALL' && user.role !== role`. It compares each listed user's role to the dropdown value, so it filters table rows. It grants or denies no access. `<Authorization>` and `checkAccess` only answer whether the signed-in user may do something, so they can't express this filter. The admin-only restriction is still enforced by the `<Authorization allowedRoles={[ROLES.ADMIN]}>` wrapper in the route.
- **Proposed rule change, if you agree:** exclude data-filtering code from the rule. One option is to skip comparisons made inside `.filter()` callbacks or in `utils/filter-*.ts` files. The test case would be `users.filter((u) => u.role === role)`, which should pass. `if (user.role === 'ADMIN') return true` should still fail.

I haven't touched the rule, its config or any ignore comments. I also haven't dodged the check by restructuring the comparison, because that would hide the pattern without changing what the code does.
